Alex — thanks for the quick report and the pcap. We've looped in Karthik (net infra) and Monica (CS on-call). A quick initial read: this matches classic MTU/MSS fragmentation failure patterns we see when a path enforces a smaller MTU but there's no PMTUD response getting through (ICMP blocked), or when an intermediate device is doing MSS clamping inconsistently.

Immediate asks:
1) Can you share the traceroute from the failing host to the target (including TTL-expire hops) and a tcpdump from the Redwood edge within the same timeframe?
2) Do you have any firewall rules that would block ICMP type 3/code 4 (fragmentation needed) back to your hosts?
3) Any recent changes to SNAT / port preservation on your egress? (we want to rule out port exhaustion interaction later)

Proposed short timeline:
- Karthik will triage the pcap and confirm whether packets are being fragmented/black-holed.
- If we see MTU issues, we'll propose a temporary MSS clamp on the Redwood edge (can do per-route) and schedule an MTU-friendly config for the maintenance window.

Karthik, Monica — tagging you for standup and to decide if we should spin up a bridge now. Alex — please drop the traceroute and a host-side tcpdump (capture on upload) to the Drive link in HS-81427, and we'll pull logs from our edge.

Subject: RE: Problems after private cutover: large-packet uploads failing

Summary of findings after triage of supplied pcaps and our edge logs:

- Evidence: Host-side pcap shows multiple packets with DF (Don't Fragment) flagged and MSS ~1460. The host begins to retransmit after a sequence of unacked segments; eventually session sees TCP RST.
- Redwood edge capture shows packets of size ~1500 arriving, but we do NOT see any ICMP 'fragmentation needed' messages returning to the host — consistent with upstream ICMP filtering at the colo.
- Path MTU: there's an intermediate hop (colo -> equinix) that has MTU 1400 on the transit segment between colo and Redwood's interconnect (we can reproduce via targeted traceroute with packet sizes). That MTU was tolerated when packets were fragmented, but because DF is set and ICMP is filtered, PMTUD fails and the connection stalls.

Immediate mitigations (recommended):
1) Temporary: Apply MSS clamp of 1360 on the Redwood ingress for Clearline CIDRs (per-route) — this will avoid reliance on PMTUD and should restore reliability immediately. I can push this within 5–10 minutes after you sign off.
2) Mid-term: Work with colo provider to allow ICMP type 3/code 4 from our interconnect to your hosts so PMTUD can function.
3) Long-term: Schedule a maintenance window to normalise MTU on the transit segment or provision jumbo-friendly path where needed.

Additional notes: we validated there are no SNAT port exhaustion symptoms in our metrics for the affected period; port utilization well within targets. Also confirmed SG/firewall rules on Redwood side are permissive for ICMP; blocking is on the colo path per your note.

Action items / next steps:
- Alex/Jesse: confirm you want us to apply the MSS clamp now (we suggest 1360) — we will monitor uploads for a 30-minute window and rollback if any regressions.
- Clearline to open a ticket with colo to allow ICMP fragmentation-needed back to hosts (we'll provide the exact flow-ids).
- Monica: I'll hand the post-mitigation communication to CS for change log and RCA draft.

If agreed, I'll enqueue the clamp and notify once live.
